title: Increasing Classroom Participation and Improving Writing: Self-Regulated Strategy Instruction
abstract: Background Two challenges that psychology faculty face are encouraging classroom participation and improving writing. Objective This article details the implementation of self-assessment, goal setting, and reflection activities to increase classroom participation and improve writing. Method The sample includes 25 students in a developmental psychology course. At the start of the term, students were asked to write two participation goals and two writing goals, and to reflect on them during the term. Pre- and postsurveys and student reflections were analyzed. Results All students met at least two of their goals. Themes that emerged from the qualitative analysis include: (1) participation and writing can be improved with practice and become easier over time; (2) these skills are interconnected; and (3) writing specific and realistic goals that are revisited frequently benefits students. Conclusion This study shows that psychology students can be taught to become more self-regulated learners through self-assessment, goal setting, and self-reflection activities. Teaching Implications Teaching self-regulation skills related to participation and writing is an effective instructional strategy for increasing classroom participation and improving writing in psychology courses.
